snippet.title: Lost Sight, Not Vision | Bhavesh Bhatia | Zomato
snippet.description:
He might have lost his eyesight but hasn't lost his vision. Meet Bhavesh Bhatia, the founder of Sunrise Candles.

Born in a small room in Mahabaleshwar and raised by a single mother, he grew up knowing two things i.e. struggle and strength. When he slowly began losing his eyesight in his teens, people told him life would get darker from here. Instead, he decided to create light for others.

From starting with selling candles on a cart in Mahabaleshwar to helping 10,000 visually impaired people find employment with his venture, it is business as usual for Bhavesh.

#Zomato #FoodDelivery #OnlineOrdering #Hustle #FuelYourHustle #Inspiration #Bhavesh #BhaveshBhatia #SunriseCandles #Mahabaleshwar #Entrepreneur

A big thank you to NEPRA our waste management partner for 2024.

In this episode of Breaking Bread, we meet Varun Tuli, Founder and MD of The Yum Yum Tree Group. The group has restaurants like Yum Yum Cha, PotPot, Tbsp, Wheaty - which are all forerunners in innovating culinary experiences for its patrons.

Varun is super passionate and his drive to innovate never dies. Join us as we talk about the learnings he’s had while running one of Delhi’s best restaurants and how he and his team are innovating in their category to stand out and build legendary brands.

snippet.title: Breaking Bread S2E4 | Learn nightlife industry's secret sauce | Deepinder Goyal ft. Priyank Sukhija
snippet.description:
MisoSexy, Noche, Lord of the Drinks, Diablo, Tamasha, are some of the iconic places that top the list of most loved restaurants and bars, but did you know that all these places (and a lot more) belong to one person – Priyank Sukhija.

In this episode of Breaking Bread, Priyank Sukhija shares some trade secrets of the nightlife industry. We also discuss some challenges in this space, and why having a great nightlife scene is important for tourism in India.

snippet.title: Breaking Bread S2E3 | How to make it in the hospitality industry? Deepinder Goyal ft. Anahita Dhondy
snippet.description:
In this episode of Breaking Bread, we explore the culinary journey of Anahita Dhondy, an acclaimed chef and author from India, who trained at hotel management in Aurangabad and Le Cordon Bleu.

Anahita is passionate about preserving her Parsi food culture, which is rich in flavors from India’s Zoroastrian community. At just 23 years old, Anahita became a chef manager at SodaBottleOpenerWala, where she cooked up authentic Parsi dishes and helped with expansion. Join us as we uncover her story of culinary creativity and discuss what it takes to build a restaurant in an ever-changing environment.
